atom.description: Swift is designed so that the simple form is the default, and complexity is opted into one feature at a time. A user can write `let x = 1` before they know about types; they can write `func f() { ... }` before they know about access control; they can write a `struct` before they need a `protocol`; they can use `try` before they need typed throws; they can call `f()` before they need `await`. Each feature waits until it is actually needed and only then enters the user's code.
